Reading 10x Genomics data into Seurat objects

Source: vignettes/seuratFrom10x.Rmd
seuratFrom10x.Rmd
library(rscprep)
library(Seurat)

seuratFrom10x() handles the two shapes 10x Cell Ranger output actually comes in – standard single-sample cellranger count runs, and demuxed cellranger multi runs – behind one interface, so downstream code doesn’t need to branch on which one it’s looking at.

You can point it at a single sample or run directly, or hand it a manifest describing a batch of runs from either pipeline. Either way, it returns a named list of Seurat objects, one per sample, ready to merge or process independently.

The multi argument is the one thing you have to get right, and it asks which pipeline wrote the directory – not whether samples were pooled. See “Choosing multi” below if the run came off cellranger multi with a single sample in it, which is the usual shape for Flex and 5’.

The example data

Every example in this vignette runs on data bundled with rscprep: a cut-down copy of the 10x Genomics demo run 1k Heart Cells from an E18 Mouse (v3 chemistry). It is one sample from one cellranger count run (Cell Ranger 3.0.0, mm10 reference), with all 1,011 cells Cell Ranger called.

It comes in two forms, holding the same data:

  • heart1k – a Seurat object, for examples that start after loading.
  • A Cell Ranger outs/ directory – for the functions that take a path. It holds filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 (the called cells) and raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5 (every barcode that had at least 25 UMIs in the original run, empty droplets included):
outs <- system.file("extdata", "heart_1k_v3", "outs", package = "rscprep")

To keep the package small, only 2,092 of the 31,053 genes are kept: the 2,000 detected in the most cells, plus every mitochondrial, ribosomal protein and cell-cycle gene. Each cell therefore keeps about 70% of its UMIs, and percentages such as pctMito read higher than they would on the full gene set. That is fine for showing how the functions behave and wrong for drawing conclusions about heart tissue. ?heart1k has the details, and data-raw/heart_1k_v3.R in the package source rebuilds it from the 10x download.

A cellranger count run 

seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(
  path  = outs,
  multi = FALSE
)
#> ✔ "heart_1k_v3": 957 cells, 2089 features.
#> ✔ Loaded 1 sample.

seurat_list$heart_1k_v3
#> An object of class Seurat 
#> 2089 features across 957 samples within 1 assay 
#> Active assay: RNA (2089 features, 0 variable features)
#>  1 layer present: counts

path should point to the Cell Ranger outs/ directory – the function looks for filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 directly inside it. The sample name is inferred from the parent folder (heart_1k_v3, one level up from outs).

That object has 957 cells, not the 1,011 in heart1k. The defaults min.cells = 10 and min.features = 50 are passed to Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(), and with only ~2,000 genes in the bundled matrix, 54 cells fall under 50 detected genes. heart1k was built with both set to 0 so it keeps every cell Cell Ranger called:

seuratFrom10x(path = outs, multi = FALSE, min.cells = 0, min.features = 0)
#> ✔ "heart_1k_v3": 1011 cells, 2092 features.
#> ✔ Loaded 1 sample.
#> $heart_1k_v3
#> An object of class Seurat 
#> 2092 features across 1011 samples within 1 assay 
#> Active assay: RNA (2092 features, 0 variable features)
#>  1 layer present: counts

A cellranger multi run

The bundled data comes from cellranger count, so the next two examples use placeholder paths and are not run.

seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(
  path  = "/path/to/Pool1/outs",
  multi = TRUE
)

names(seurat_list)
#> [1] "Bleo_18_Slim_10" "Bleo_22_Slim_14" ...

For cellranger multi output, one outs/ directory holds every demuxed sample under per_sample_outs/<sample>/. seuratFrom10x() reads each sample’s count/sample_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 separately and returns one Seurat object per demuxed sample – a single function call here returns a list, not a single object.

A batch of runs via manifest 

manifest <- data.frame(
  Path = c(
    "/path/to/Sample_1/outs",
    "/path/to/Sample_2/outs",
    "/path/to/Pool1/outs"
  ),
  multi = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)
)

seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(manifest = manifest, min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)

The manifest needs a Path column (each row’s outs/ directory) and a logical multi column. Rows can mix the two pipelines freely – each row is resolved independently, and a multi = TRUE row expands into one entry per demuxed sample in the returned list. If a sample’s expected H5 file is missing, that row is skipped with a warning rather than failing the whole batch; single-path mode fails immediately instead, since there’s nothing left to fall back on.

Choosing multi

multi picks between two directory layouts, and the two Cell Ranger pipelines write different ones:

multi Pipeline Where the filtered H5 lives
FALSE cellranger count outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5
TRUE cellranger multi outs/per_sample_outs/<sample>/count/sample_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5

The question is which pipeline ran, not how many samples came out of it. cellranger multi writes per_sample_outs/ even when it demultiplexed exactly one sample – routine for Flex and 5’ – so those runs need multi = TRUE despite not being multiplexed in any biological sense. If you are unsure, look for per_sample_outs/ inside outs/: if it is there, the run needs multi = TRUE.

This argument used to be called multiplexed, which read as a claim about the experiment rather than about the pipeline. The old name still works and warns.

Notes

min.cells and min.features are passed straight through to Seurat::CreateSeuratObject() and apply uniformly across every sample in a batch – set them once at the level of granularity you actually want, not per-sample.
